div.div: 🩻 Static device gone rogue on DHCP

p.i: „Ein Röntgengerät ist letzte Woche ausgestiegen, weil die IP-Adresse aus unerklärlichen Gründen auf DHCP umgestellt wurde, was zu längerer Ursachenbehebung geführt hat."

div.p: A device that must keep a fixed IP was silently switched to DHCP, got a new address, and dropped off the imaging network — hours lost finding out why. Splunk catches it the moment it happens: a static-assigned device that takes a DHCP lease. Correlate DHCP (the lease), NAC/ISE (which device & profile), the asset inventory (it should be static), and NetFlow (the imaging traffic that broke).

panel.title: Devices currently on a DHCP lease

single.option: incl. devices meant to be static

panel.title: 🚨 The smoking gun — static devices that took a DHCP lease

search.query: | where violation=="YES" | eval Impact=if(criticality=="Critical","● Critical — patient-facing","● High") | rename device as Device, criticality as Criticality, site as Site, expected_ip as "Expected static IP", dhcp_ip as "Actual DHCP IP", lease_min as "Lease (min)", switchport as Switchport, detected as "First seen on DHCP" | table Device Criticality Site "Expected static IP" "Actual DHCP IP" "Lease (min)" Switchport "First seen on DHCP" Impact

panel.title: DHCP lease activity (7 days) — violations spike above the baseline

search.query: | makeresults count=84 | streamstats count as h | eval _time=now()-(84-h)*7200 | eval "Normal DHCP leases"=10+(h%7)*2 | eval "Static-device violations"=case(h==61,1, h==78,1, true(),0) | timechart span=12h sum("Normal DHCP leases") as "Normal DHCP leases" sum("Static-device violations") as "Static-device violations"

panel.title: NetFlow impact — XRAY-BER-01 traffic to PACS hands off to the new IP

search.query: | makeresults count=48 | streamstats count as i | eval _time=now()-(48-i)*1800 | eval "From static IP 198.18.3.40 (KB/s)"=if(i<=30, 480+(i*4), 0) | eval "From new DHCP IP 198.18.3.187 (KB/s)"=if(i>30, 120+((i-30)*18), 0) | timechart span=30m max("From static IP 198.18.3.40 (KB/s)") as "From static IP 198.18.3.40 (KB/s)" max("From new DHCP IP 198.18.3.187 (KB/s)") as "From new DHCP IP 198.18.3.187 (KB/s)"

html.h3: Data inputs for this use case

tr.td: The lease itself: MAC → new IP, lease time, hostname. ISC dhcpd, Windows DHCP, Infoblox, or Cisco IOS DHCP.
Endpoint profile ("Medical / X-ray"), 802.1X/MAB auth, switchport, VLAN, posture — turns a MAC into "the X-ray". RADIUS accounting.
Which devices must be static, their reserved IP and criticality. This lab already ships asset lookups (Infra Monitoring ▸ Asset Config).
Shows the device's traffic to PACS/imaging dropping on the old IP and resuming on the new one. Great "why it broke" evidence; not needed to detect.
DHCP-snooping binding changes and dynamic-DNS re-registration corroborate the flip.

html.h3: The real detection search (once DHCP + asset are onboarded)
html.p: The panels above use inline sample data so the story renders with no ingestion. With a real DHCP feed and the asset lookup, the core detection is a single correlation search — schedule it as an alert (→ Webex):
html.pre: index=* sourcetype=isc:dhcp (DHCPACK OR DHCPREQUEST) | rex "DHCP(ACK|REQUEST).*?(?<dhcp_ip>\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+).*?(?<mac>([0-9a-f]{2}:){5}[0-9a-f]{2})" | stats latest(_time) as last latest(dhcp_ip) as dhcp_ip by mac | lookup dcloud_assets_berlin_lk mac OUTPUT device expected_ip addressing criticality | lookup dcloud_assets_london_lk mac OUTPUT device expected_ip addressing criticality | where addressing="static" AND dhcp_ip!=expected_ip | eval detected=strftime(last,"%F %T") | table detected device criticality mac expected_ip dhcp_ip
html.p: (Optionally join NAC/ISE on mac for the endpoint profile + switchport, and NetFlow on the IPs for the impact chart.)
